Pareto-optimal routes trading cost against a resource

Source: R/routing.R
ox_route_pareto.Rd

Enumerates the routes from from to to that are Pareto-optimal in two criteria: the routing weight (cost) and a second nonnegative edge column (resource), typically a road-type penalty from ox_add_edge_penalties(). Each returned route is cheaper than the next and uses more resource than the next; no other route is better on both criteria. The front is computed exactly in the Rust core by bicriteria label-setting (Martins' algorithm) with dominance pruning and reverse-Dijkstra bounds.

Usage

ox_route_pareto(
  g,
  from,
  to,
  weight = "length",
  resource,
  budget = Inf,
  max_routes = Inf
)

Arguments

g

An osm_graph.

from, to

Node osmids (as returned by ox_nearest_nodes()).

weight

Edge column used as routing cost. Default "length".

resource

Name of a nonnegative edge column holding the second criterion, e.g. the "penalty" column of ox_add_edge_penalties().

budget

Keep only routes with total resource at most budget. Default Inf (the unrestricted front).

max_routes

Return at most this many routes (the cheapest ones). Default Inf.

Value

An sf tibble with one row per Pareto-optimal route, ordered by increasing cost (and decreasing resource): route (rank), cost, resource, a list-column path of the node osmids traversed, and the route's merged street geometry.

Details

With a finite budget the front is restricted to routes whose total resource is at most budget; its first row is then the exact solution of the constrained shortest path problem (see ox_route_constrained()).

The bicriteria problem is NP-hard in general — the front can be large on pathological inputs — but on street networks with sparse penalties the pruned search is fast. Use max_routes to cap the enumeration.

Examples

g <- example_osm_graph()
# north-south streets are calm residential, east-west ones primary
g$edges$highway <- ifelse(abs(g$edges$u - g$edges$v) == 1, "residential", "primary")
g <- ox_add_edge_penalties(g, c(residential = 1))
from <- ox_nearest_nodes(g, 0, 0)
to <- ox_nearest_nodes(g, 300, 300)
ox_route_pareto(g, from, to, resource = "penalty")
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 4 fields
#> Geometry type: LINESTRING
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 300 ymax: 300
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   route  cost resource path                                             geometry
#>   <int> <dbl>    <dbl> <list>                                   <LINESTRING [m]>
#> 1     1   600      300 <int [7]> (0 0, 100 0, 200 0, 200 100, 300 100, 300 200,…
